The app follows your phone’s language (English or Spanish). On Android 13 and later you can also change it in your phone’s app settings.
Remoto is not affiliated with or sponsored by the manufacturers mentioned in the app.

Remoto works in two ways:

• Wi-Fi: your phone and your TV must be on the same Wi-Fi network. The first time, the TV asks you to approve the connection.
• Infrared: only on phones with an IR blaster. Point the top of the phone at the TV.

No TV at hand? Choose “Try without a TV” to explore every button with a simulated TV.

The simulated TV lives inside the app and doesn’t use your network. Every button you press shows a reaction on its screen.\n\nTo see how Remoto handles problems, tap the bug icon at the top of the remote and choose an error.
The TV didn’t answer in time

Check that:

• The TV is on (some TVs turn off their network a few minutes after you switch them off).
• Your phone and your TV are on the same Wi-Fi network, not a guest network.
• Your router doesn’t isolate devices from each other (sometimes called “AP isolation” or “client isolation”).

Then tap “Try again”.

The code didn’t match or the request was declined on the TV.

• Tap “Try again” and type the code exactly as it appears on the TV.
• If the TV shows a request, accept it with its original remote.
• If you declined it before, some TVs remember that: look for “connected devices” or “device manager” in the TV’s settings and allow Remoto.

Recent versions of Android ask for permission before an app can talk to devices on your home network, such as your TV.

To allow it: open your phone’s Settings › Apps › Remoto › Permissions › Nearby devices, and choose Allow. Then come back and tap “Try again”.

Remoto only uses this permission to talk to your TV. Your list of devices never leaves your phone.
To control a TV over the network, connect your phone to the same Wi-Fi network as the TV. Mobile data doesn’t work for this.\n\nIf your phone has an infrared blaster, you can use infrared instead.

The TV isn’t answering at its usual address.

• Turn the TV on with its original remote and try again.
• If your router gave the TV a new address, search your Wi-Fi again.
• Restarting the router can also help.
